text_1.text: Ambarella’s technologies make cameras smarter - enabling features like person detection, object classification, analytics, and more - performing complex data analysis in real time, delivering breathtaking imagery, and preserving vital system resources such as power and network bandwidth. Ambarella specializes in the development of deployable, scalable designs for intelligent cameras, offering a proven path to mass production. Check out our Ambarella products, SoCs, CPUs, chipsets, and more.

What is Ambarella CVflow architecture?

CVflow is Ambarella’s computer vision chip architecture. Unlike a general-purpose CPU or GPU, it uses a dedicated vision processing engine programmed with a high-level algorithm description. That design scales performance to trillions of operations per second at very low power.

Which neural network frameworks do Ambarella SoCs support?

Customers map CNNs trained with industry-standard tools such as Caffe, TensorFlow, and PyTorch onto Ambarella processors. The CNN toolkit also covers ONNX. Detection, classification, and related CNN/DNN tasks run on-chip.

Which Ambarella SoCs are used for ADAS?

CV2FS is for front-facing stereovision ADAS cameras and computer-vision ECUs at L2+ and higher, with CVflow AI and ASIL C compliance. CV22FS targets forward-facing monocular ADAS cameras and similar ECUs, also with ASIL C. Ambarella uses ISO 26262 processes for functional safety–certified products used in ADAS and autonomous driving.

What makes Ambarella a low-power edge AI SoC choice?

The SoCs and CPUs are built for embedded edge platforms such as battery-powered cameras. They can outperform competing solutions on power efficiency, sometimes by 5× or more, while matching or beating results. Compression also cuts bandwidth and storage.

What does stereovision add for robotics?

Stereo processing turns a 2D view into a 3D scene and can detect generic obstacles the system was not trained to recognize. CV2 is positioned for accurate 3D environmental modeling, real-time neural network performance, advanced robotics, and industrial autonomous robots.

title_1.jcr:title: Ambarella N1 Family - Edge GenAI Is Here

text_1.text:
Ambarella’s N1 family of Edge GenAI SoCs delivers the processing power needed to run multimodal large language models (LLMs), vision-language models (VLMs), and traditional CNN networks locally, without cloud dependency. Designed for autonomous mobile robots, on-premise AI boxes, smart city security, industrial automation, and intelligent healthcare, the N1 series sets a new benchmark for AI performance per watt at the edge.

As an authorized Ambarella distributor and value-added engineering partner, Macnica Americas provides component supply, design-in support, and technical consulting to help you bring your next N1-based design to production.

item2.text: Key Features of Ambarella SoC Products

textwithimage_1.text:
CVflow® Chip Architecture

Ambarella CVflow® chip architecture is based on a deep understanding of core computer vision algorithms. Unlike general-purpose CPUs and GPUs, CVflow includes a dedicated vision processing engine programmed with a high-level algorithm description, allowing Ambarella architecture to scale performance to trillions of operations per second with extremely low power consumption.

With CVflow, customers can efficiently map their own CNN networks trained with industry-standard tools (e.g., Caffe, TensorFlow, PyTorch) to run on Ambarella processors.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Stereovision

Stereo processing transforms the world from a flat 2D plane into a full 3D environment. This not only provides a richer, denser representation of the target scene, but also allows the detection of generic obstacles that the system hasn’t been trained to recognize, making navigation safer and more effective for warehouse robots, autonomous vehicles, and more.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Low Power

Ambarella technology products are designed to be deployed in embedded platforms on the edge (e.g., battery-powered cameras), where power consumption is a critical concern. Ambarella SoCs and CPUs consistently outperform competitive solutions in power efficiency - sometimes by 5x or more - while delivering equal or superior results.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Reduce Bandwidth & Storage Costs

Ambarella compression technologies dramatically reduce data transmission size, slashing storage costs and bandwidth usage with Ambarella products.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Image Quality

One of the hallmarks of Ambarella processors is our image processing pipeline. Encompassing everything from HDR to EIS to dewarping, our state-of-the-art ISP ensures that every frame of every video is exquisite, improving safety and enhancing the viewing experience.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Autonomy

From drones to robots, from taxis to long-haul semi trucks, Ambarella’s vision processors were designed to revolutionize the way we work and travel. Our hardware platforms deliver the flexibility required to implement all levels of automation, including partial, conditional, high, and full autonomy.

text_1.text: <hr />

textwithimage_1.text:
Functional Safety

As an AI silicon company offering SoCs for applications such as ADAS and autonomous driving, Ambarella has implemented an array of internal processes and procedures to ensure that their functional safety-certified products comply with ISO 26262. These strict processes and procedures touch every aspect of the work Ambarella does - from technical documentation to software engineering to VLSI - and have become an inextricable part of Ambarella culture, from top to bottom.

text_1.text: <hr />

CV72S

The Ambarella CV72S SoC's combination of high performance and low power consumption makes it an ideal solution for various applications, including automotive, security cameras, drones, and other intelligent vision systems.

CV2

Designed for accurate 3D environmental modeling and real-time neural network performance, the CV2 chip enables advanced robotics and industrial applications, including autonomous robots.

CV2FS

Designed for front-facing stereovision ADAS cameras, as well as computer vision ECUs for L2+ and higher levels of autonomy, the CV2FS chip features CVflow® AI processing and ASIL C compliance to enable safety-critical applications.

CV20AQ

Featuring CVflow® AI processing, the CV20AQ chip targets stereo-camera advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), multi-camera L2+ systems, multi-camera driver monitoring systems (DMS) and occupancy monitoring solutions (OMS), multi-channel electronic mirrors with blind spot detection, and intelligent parking assistance systems.

CV22

Ambarella’s CV22 SoC combines advanced image processing with our powerful CVflow® computer vision architecture to deliver the next generation of intelligent robotics and industrial applications.

CV22AQ

The CV22AQ delivers next-generation image processing, 12MP30 video encoding, and CVflow® computer vision performance in an optimized, low-power design.

CV22FS

Featuring CVflow® AI processing and ASIL C compliance to enable safety-critical applications, the CV22FS chip targets forward-facing monocular ADAS cameras, as well as computer vision ECUs for L2+ and higher levels of autonomy.

CV25

The CV25 chip combines advanced image processing and real-time CVflow® computer vision performance for intelligent industrial/robotics applications.

CV25AQ

With the lowest power consumption in the CVflow® family, the CV25AQ combines advanced image processing, 6MP30 video encoding, and CVflow computer vision performance.

CV28AQ

Ambarella’s AEC-Q100 qualified CV28AQ SoC combines image processing, 6MP30 video encoding/decoding, and CVflow® computer vision processing in a single, low-power design, making it an ideal choice to power the next generation of intelligent automotive.

CV28M

Our CV28M SoC is designed for intelligent applications at the edge, including smart home security, retail monitoring, consumer robotics, and occupancy monitoring. The chip’s high-performance CVflow® architecture provides deep neural network (DNN) computer vision processing and 4KP30 video encoding, enabling an array of computer vision-based devices.

H22AQ

An industry-leading combination of low power and high performance, the H22AQ SoC delivers image/video processing and 8MP30 video encoding/decoding in a single design.

H32AQ

The H32AQ SoC combines 6MP30 video encoding, image/video processing, and a quad-core processor in a single, low-power design.

A12AQ

Engineered for electronic mirrors and automotive video recording systems, the A12AQ processor provides superior visibility even in low-light or high-contrast environments, delivering a combination of advanced image processing, high dynamic range (HDR), 3D noise filtering, smart auto exposure, and high-resolution encode performance.

title_1.jcr:title: Why Edge AI? The Case for Local Processing

text_1.text:
Cloud-based AI inference is facing real headwinds: bandwidth costs, ongoing service fees, latency constraints, data privacy regulations, and connectivity limitations in the field. The Ambarella N1 family is purpose-built for the shift toward edge-native AI, where the intelligence lives in the device rather than in a remote data center.

Ambarella’s CVflow® architecture and fine-tuning techniques, including QLoRA-based model compression, make it possible to run production-grade GenAI models in power-and-cost-constrained enclosures. The result is a new class of intelligent edge device that responds faster, costs less to operate, and is more secure by design.

The N1-655’s combination of multi-channel video decode, VLM support, and sub-20W power envelope makes it well suited for AMRs that need to interpret complex environments, respond to natural language commands, and operate continuously without a cloud connection.

From AI visual inspection to collaborative robots on the production line, the N1 family supports the multi-sensor, real-time processing that modern manufacturing requires. Both SoCs integrate naturally into AIoT architectures where data stays on the factory floor.

Process multiple camera feeds simultaneously, run object detection, classification, and tracking alongside VLM-based scene understanding, all within a single manageable power budget. Eliminate recurring cloud processing costs for large-scale deployments.

title_1.jcr:title: On-Premise AI Boxes and Edge Servers

text_1.text: For enterprises that cannot or will not send sensitive video and sensor data to the cloud, the N1 family enables full-featured GenAI inference to run locally in a standard rack, an industrial enclosure, or an edge appliance.

High-resolution imaging, real-time diagnostics support, and patient data that never leaves the facility. The N1’s processing depth and sensor fusion capabilities address the demanding requirements of edge medical AI.

title_2.jcr:title: Multi-modal 3D facial recognition for secure, privacy-compliant access control

text_1.text: NAMUGA is a global innovator in advanced camera modules and 3D sensing solutions, delivering ultra-compact, high-performance imaging technologies for some of the world’s most demanding applications. Founded in 2004 and headquartered in South Korea, NAMUGA combines advanced optics, sensing, AI-enabled imaging, and automated manufacturing expertise to help customers accelerate intelligent vision system development.

Vicon Lite is a vision-powered access control terminal developed by Namuga, drawing on more than 20 years of camera and sensing module expertise. Where conventional access control relies on cards, PINs, or centralized biometric databases, Vicon Lite replaces that model with multi-modal 3D facial recognition, on-device AI processing, and post-quantum encryption, delivering fast, accurate, and privacy-respecting authentication at the door.

Built on Namuga's NEPS platform, Vicon Lite brings together four capabilities that most access control systems treat as separate problems: strong biometric authentication, data sovereignty for the user, quantum-resistant security for data in transit and at rest, and plug-and-play deployment into existing RFID infrastructure. The result is a single compact terminal that handles every access challenge without added complexity or facility downtime.

Macnica Americas is an authorized distributor of Namuga and Vicon Lite in North America, providing customers with local technical support, system integration guidance, and access to Namuga's engineering resources.
Vicon Lite unifies the security, privacy, and deployment requirements that typically require multiple systems into a single compact terminal.

image_1.alt: Namuga Pinocchio dual-lens stereo depth RGB/IR camera banner

text_1.text: Vicon Lite uses stereo RGB and IR cameras to cross-validate depth, skin, and blood flow in real time. Photos, videos, and masks do not pass. The system achieves 99.7% recognition accuracy with a 0.3-second authentication speed, and supports facial vein recognition and gesture-based multi-factor authentication in the Pro model.

title_1.jcr:title: Post-Quantum Encryption via the NEPS Platform

text_1.text: Every layer of the Vicon Lite system is protected by the NEPS platform: ML-DSA and AES-256 encryption, PUF-based device key enclave for hardware-level protection, and TLS 1.3 for secure communications. This architecture provides protection against both current and emerging cryptographic threats, and is GDPR and CCPA compliant by design.

Biometric data never enters a central server. Vicon Lite uses a Self-Sovereign Identity architecture in which users carry their own encrypted identity. Users can enroll, update, or delete their biometric data at any time, giving individuals direct control over their own credentials. On-device 1:1 matching is the default mode, with 1:N matching available for enterprise deployments.

Vicon Lite integrates with any existing RFID environment in hours. No new wiring, no additional software installation, and zero facility downtime during deployment. A built-in web server handles device management without requiring separate software, and the system supports 1:1, 1:N, and hybrid authentication modes.

title_1.jcr:title: One Device. Every Access Challenge Solved.

text_1.text: Vicon Lite addresses three categories of access control challenge that traditional systems handle inadequately:

image_1.alt: Namuga Stella180 Solid State On-Device LiDAR banner

text_1.text: From the hardware key enclave to the cloud, every layer of the Vicon Lite system is protected by post-quantum encryption. Identity data in storage and in transit is secured against both present-day attacks and future cryptographic threats, making Vicon Lite future-proof from day one.

A single tap on a smartphone authenticates a user instantly via secure Bluetooth. No setup, no PIN, no physical card. The mobile ID capability leverages secure Bluetooth connection for biometric mobile access, reducing both friction and credential management overhead.

All facial recognition and anomaly detection runs directly on the Vicon Lite device. There is no cloud dependency, no recognition latency from round-trip processing, and no biometric data leaving the premises. The on-device AI also supports anti-tailgating analysis, detecting suspicious access behavior through AI-based behavior analysis.

Reliable Signal Distribution for Precision Timing Architectures

In advanced electronic systems, precision timing doesn't stop at the oscillator. It must be cleanly and consistently distributed across multiple clock domains. SiTime’s MEMS-based clock buffers provide high fan-out, low additive jitter, and robust performance under demanding environmental and EMI conditions. Designed to work seamlessly with SiTime’s programmable oscillators and clock generators, these buffers maintain signal integrity across harsh environments while reducing design complexity. From 5G radios to industrial robotics, SiTime's buffers are the glue that holds your timing tree together.

textwithimage_1.text:
Precision Network Synchronization for IEEE 1588/PTP

SiTime’s network synchronizers support nanosecond-level synchronization in distributed systems, enabling accurate timing across communications infrastructure - even under harsh environments and variable conditions.

title_2.jcr:title: Nanosecond Accuracy, MEMS Reliability, Network-Wide Timing Confidence

text_1.text: As next-gen networks demand tighter timing across distributed architectures, the TimeSync™ Platform from SiTime delivers industry-leading precision and robustness for IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP), Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE), and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) holdover. Unlike traditional quartz-based synchronizers, TimeSync™ integrates MEMS oscillators, DPLLs, and hitless switching logic in a compact, programmable device - resulting in superior resilience, smaller footprint, and longer holdover performance, even in harsh or mobile environments.

• Integrated DPLL + MEMS Oscillator: Combines digital phase-locked loop with rugged MEMS timing for sub-microsecond alignment under variable network conditions
  • Hitless Reference Switching: Maintains continuous, undisturbed operation during timing source transitions or failures
  • Precision Holdover: Maintains network sync with nanosecond-level accuracy even during GNSS loss, ideal for edge and indoor deployments
  • Multi-Protocol Support: Supports full Synchronous Ethernet and IEEE 1588 PTP timing stacks for a variety of telecom and datacom standards
  • Compact Footprint: Designed for space-constrained systems including small cells, fronthaul gateways, microwave backhaul, and C-RAN infrastructure
<hr />

text_1.text:
The defect that stops your line is smaller than most cameras can resolve

Canon's LI8030SA puts 410 million pixels behind the lens, giving automated and robotic inspection systems the resolution to catch what conventional vision hardware misses, from a full wafer down to a single micro bump.

Sensor status: In development at Canon. Macnica is scoping early samples and design in timelines now. Contact us to get on the list.

As packaging goes 3D, the defects that matter go microscopic

Advanced GPU and AI chips now stack dies with HBM, larger logic, and dense interposers. Every TSV, RDL trace, and micro bump adds another point of possible failure, and one bad connection can take the whole package down. Panel and chip unit costs are high enough that zero failure is the only acceptable target, which means inspection has to cover every connection, not a sample of them.

Most vision systems trade resolution for speed, or speed for field of view. On a full wafer or a large format package, that tradeoff is exactly where defects hide.

textwithimage_1.text:
One capture, an entire panel, in focus

LI8030SA is a back illuminated, stacked CMOS sensor with a redesigned readout architecture, built specifically for applications where resolution and field of view can no longer be a tradeoff. The monochrome variant adds 4 pixel binning, so the same sensor can drop to 100MP at 24fps when throughput matters more than maximum detail.

textwithimage_1.text:
Built for the inspection tasks a standard sensor has to walk away from

From Canon's own target market analysis, LI8030SA is being validated across six application areas where full field resolution and micron level detail decide whether an inspection system catches the defect or misses it.

text_1.text:
Wafer & chip production inspection

Resolve defects across an entire wafer in one capture, instead of stitching together dozens of narrower field images.

2.5D / 3D package inspection

Check TSV, RDL, and micro bump structures down to roughly 25 to 30 micron features, where a single bad connection fails the whole package.

Astronomical observation

Wide field of view paired with high resolution, so faint or distant objects stay resolvable across the full frame.

Microbial and bacterial detection

Cell level detail for bio and medical testing workflows that depend on resolving structures far below the millimeter scale.

Wide area monitoring & license plate recognition

Cover more ground per camera, with resolution to spare for identification tasks like plate recognition at range.

Simultaneous, full panel inspection

Inspect many parts, dies, or components in a single frame instead of indexing a camera across each one individually.

textwithimage_1.text:
Sensor resolution only matters if the lens can deliver it

Macnica has already qualified multiple telecentric and high-resolution lens options for LI8030SA, so you're choosing from proven optical paths instead of starting a lens search from zero. The right option depends on your working distance, feature size, and field of view, and that's exactly the conversation our applications team has with you before any hardware is spec’ed.
